I will make you a great nation, I will bless you and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse those who curse you; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.

You shall be a father of many nations. I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come from you. And I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations, for an everlasting covenant.

Blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your descendants as the stars of the heaven and as the sand which is on the seashore; and your descendants shall possess the gate of their enemies.
Dwell in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and your descendants I give all these lands, and I will perform the oath which I swore to Avraham your father.

When you return to YHWH your Sovereign and obey his voice according to all I command you today, then YHWH your Sovereign will restore your captivity and have compassion on you, and will gather you again from all the peoples where YHWH your Sovereign has scattered you.

I will make a new covenant with the house of Yisra'EL and with the house of Yehudah — I will put my Torah in their minds and write it on their hearts; and I will be their Sovereign, and they shall be my people.

I will take the children of Yisra'EL from among the nations, wherever they have gone, and will gather them from every side and bring them into their own land; and I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Yisra'EL.
Every male among you shall be circumcised. It shall be an everlasting covenant in your flesh, a sign of the covenant between me and you throughout your generations.

Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land not their own, and they will be enslaved and afflicted four hundred years. But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they shall come out with great substance.
I will bring forth a seed out of Ya'akov, and out of Yehudah an inheritor of my mountains; my elect shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there.

The seventh day of rest established at Creation. YHWH rested on the seventh day and set it apart. Shabbat is the foundational appointed time — the covenant sign woven into the fabric of creation itself, not an institutional invention. The day itself runs sunrise to sunrise, per the DSS/Orit solar reckoning (Yovelim 3:28, 21:10, Vayikra 7:15, 22:29-30, Shemot 12:10, 23:18, 29:34, 34:25, Bamidbar 9:12, Devarim 16:4, 4QCalendrical Texts 4Q320-330); sunset-to-sunset reckoning follows Babylonian practice, not the covenant calendar.

The memorial of the night YHWH passed over the houses of Yisra'EL in Egypt. A lamb without blemish, its blood applied to the doorposts, eaten in haste. The Torah fixes Pesakh (Shemot 12) in the 1st month on the 14th day, and the DSS calendar keeps it independent of the later Rabbinic lunar system.

The Feast of Unleavened Bread, beginning the day after Pesakh and lasting seven days. No leaven found in any dwelling. A solemn assembly on the first and seventh days. Commemorates the haste of departure from Mitsrayim.

The offering of the first sheaf of the harvest — the firstfruits — brought before YHWH. No grain from the new harvest is eaten until this is done. The counting of the omer begins here, leading to Shavuot fifty days later.

The Feast of Weeks — fifty days counted from Bikkurim. A harvest festival and, per Shemot 19:1, the anniversary of the covenant at Sinai. The 364-day covenant calendar places Shavuot always on the 15th of the 3rd month, a Sunday, by the count of Vayikra 23:15-16.

The Day of Trumpets — a day of rest and a memorial of blowing. The texts give no name beyond "a holy convocation" and "a memorial of blowing." Later traditions added meanings not found in the ancient corpus. The ancient text simply commands: rest and blow.

The Day of Atonement — the most solemn of the appointed times. A complete rest, a day of affliction of the soul. The high priest entered the most set-apart place. The scapegoat ritual sent the sins of the people into the wilderness on Azazel. Described in detail in Vayikra 16.

The Feast of Tabernacles — seven days of dwelling in booths to remember that Yisra'EL dwelt in booths when brought out of Mitsrayim. The most joyful of the appointed times. A great assembly on the 8th day (Shemini Atzeret) follows the seven days.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Creation of heaven and earth
key_terms.definition: YHWH creates the world in six days; the seventh day is set apart as Shabbat.
The first man formed from the earth, the first woman from his side. Placed in the Garden of Eden.
Transgression in the garden; expulsion. The ground is cursed. Death enters.
The first murder. Qayin driven out eastward. The line of Sheth established as the covenant line.
200 Watchers led by Shemyaza swear an oath on Mount Hermon and take human wives, corrupting the earth.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: The Nephilim and corruption
key_terms.definition: Giants and corruption spread across the earth. YHWH observes that every intent of humanity is only evil continually.
Chanokh walks with YHWH 365 years and is taken — he does not die. He receives the heavenly visions recorded in the Book of Chanokh.
YHWH instructs Noakh to build the ark. The flood covers the earth for forty days. All corrupt flesh is destroyed.
YHWH establishes an eternal covenant with Noakh and all living creatures: never again shall a flood destroy the earth.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: The Table of Nations
key_terms.definition: The seventy nations descend from Noakh's three sons — Shem, Kham, and Yephet — and spread across the earth.
YHWH calls Avram out of Ur of the Chaldeans. The covenant of land, seed, and blessing is first given.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Covenant between the parts
key_terms.definition: YHWH makes a formal covenant with Avraham, predicting 400 years of oppression before deliverance.
The covenant sign given to Avraham. His name changed from Avram to Avraham.
Ya'aqov wrestles through the night and prevails. His name is changed to Yisra'EL — one who contends with EL.
Ya'aqov and his seventy descendants go down to Egypt in the time of Yosef. The 430 years of sojourn begin.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Moshe called at the burning bush
key_terms.definition: YHWH appears to Moshe at Horev and commissions him to bring Yisra'EL out of Mitsrayim.
YHWH sends ten plagues upon Mitsrayim. Pharaoh's heart is hardened. The final plague takes every firstborn of Egypt.
Yisra'EL departs Mitsrayim with great wealth. Approximately 600,000 men on foot, plus women, children, and a mixed multitude.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Crossing the Sea of Reeds
key_terms.definition: YHWH parts the sea. Yisra'EL crosses on dry ground. Pharaoh's army is drowned.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Torah given at Sinai
key_terms.definition: YHWH descends on Mount Sinai in fire. The Ten Words and the full Torah are given to Moshe. Shemot 19:1 dates the arrival at Sinai to the third month, the season the count of Vayikra 23:15-16 lands Shavuot.
While Moshe is on the mountain, the people build a golden calf. 3,000 fall by the sword of the Levites.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Forty years in the wilderness
key_terms.definition: Due to the faithlessness of the spies, the generation that left Egypt wanders forty years. None of that generation enters the land except Yehoshua and Kalev.
Under Yehoshua, Yisra'EL crosses the Yarden River and enters the land of Kena'an.
The walls of Yeriho fall after seven days of marching and the blowing of the shofar.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: The cycles of the Judges
key_terms.definition: Yisra'EL repeatedly turns from the covenant, is oppressed by enemies, cries out, and is delivered by a judge. Devorah, Gid'on, Shimshon, and others arise.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Sha'ul anointed as first king
key_terms.definition: The people demand a king. Shemu'el anoints Sha'ul of the tribe of Binyamin as first king of Yisra'EL.
YHWH rejects Sha'ul and anoints Dawid of Yehudah. The covenant of the eternal throne is given to Dawid's line.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Shlomo and the first temple
key_terms.definition: Shlomo builds the temple in Yerushalayim. At its dedication, the cloud of YHWH fills the house.
After Shlomo, the kingdom splits into Yisra'EL (north, 10 tribes) and Yehudah (south, 2 tribes).

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Eliyahu and the prophets of Ba'al
key_terms.definition: Eliyahu challenges 450 prophets of Ba'al on Mount Karmel. Fire falls. The covenant is demonstrated.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Assyrian captivity of the North
key_terms.definition: The northern kingdom of Yisra'EL is taken captive by Assyria. The ten tribes are scattered.
Yeshayahu receives visions spanning the captivity and the ultimate restoration of Yisra'EL. The Servant Songs speak of the covenant people.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Babylonian captivity of Yehudah
key_terms.definition: Nevukhadnetzar destroys Yerushalayim and the temple. Yehudah is taken to Babylon.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Yehezkel's vision of the valley of dry bones
key_terms.definition: YHWH shows Yehezkel the scattered house of Yisra'EL restored — bone to bone, flesh returning, breath entering.
A remnant returns to Yerushalayim under Ezra and Nekhemyah. The second temple is built.
A covenant community withdraws to the Yehudean wilderness near the Dead Sea, preserving ancient texts outside the emerging Rabbinic and Hellenistic control of the temple.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: DSS texts composed and preserved
key_terms.definition: The community preserves, copies, and composes texts including 4Q246, Melkhitsedeq scroll, Temple Scroll, War Scroll, and many others between approximately 250 BCE and 68 CE.

key_terms.term: Timeline Event: Roman destruction of Qumran (68 CE)
key_terms.definition: Roman forces destroy the DSS community during the Jewish-Roman War. Scrolls are hidden in the caves. They remain there until their discovery in 1946–1947.

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Shabbat?
faq.answer: name: Shabbat | timing: Every 7th day | desc: The seventh day of rest established at Creation. YHWH rested on the seventh day and set it apart. Shabbat is the foundational appointed time — the covenant sign woven into the fabric of creation itself, not an institutional invention. | refs: Bereshit 2:2-3, Shemot 20:8-11

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Pesakh?
faq.answer: name: Pesakh | timing: 14th of the 1st month, at twilight | desc: The memorial of the night YHWH passed over the houses of Yisra'EL in Egypt. A lamb without blemish, its blood applied to the doorposts, eaten in haste. The Torah fixes Pesakh (Shemot 12) in the 1st month on the 14th day, and the DSS calendar keeps it independent of the later Rabbinic lunar system. | refs: Shemot 12:1-14, Vayikra 23:5

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Chag HaMatzot?
faq.answer: name: Chag HaMatzot | timing: 15th–21st of the 1st month (7 days) | desc: The Feast of Unleavened Bread, beginning the day after Pesakh and lasting seven days. No leaven found in any dwelling. A solemn assembly on the first and seventh days. Commemorates the haste of departure from Mitsrayim. | refs: Shemot 12:15-20, Vayikra 23:6-8

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Bikkurim (Firstfruits)?
faq.answer: name: Bikkurim (Firstfruits) | timing: Day after the Shabbat within Chag HaMatzot | desc: The offering of the first sheaf of the harvest — the firstfruits — brought before YHWH. No grain from the new harvest is eaten until this is done. The counting of the omer begins here, leading to Shavuot fifty days later. | refs: Vayikra 23:9-14

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Shavuot?
faq.answer: name: Shavuot | timing: 50 days after Bikkurim (day after 7th Shabbat) | desc: The Feast of Weeks — fifty days counted from Bikkurim. A harvest festival and, per Shemot 19:1, the anniversary of the covenant at Sinai. The 364-day covenant calendar places Shavuot always on the 15th of the 3rd month, a Sunday, by the count of Vayikra 23:15-16. | refs: Vayikra 23:15-21, Shemot 19:1

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Yom Teruah?
faq.answer: name: Yom Teruah | timing: 1st of the 7th month | desc: The Day of Trumpets — a day of rest and a memorial of blowing. The texts give no name beyond "a holy convocation" and "a memorial of blowing." Later traditions added meanings not found in the ancient corpus. The ancient text simply commands: rest and blow. | refs: Vayikra 23:23-25, Bamidbar 29:1

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Yom Kippur?
faq.answer: name: Yom Kippur | timing: 10th of the 7th month | desc: The Day of Atonement — the most solemn of the appointed times. A complete rest, a day of affliction of the soul. Described in detail in Vayikra 16. | refs: Vayikra 23:26-32, Vayikra 16:1-34

faq.question: What does the Mo'edim reference give for Mo'ed: Sukkot?
faq.answer: name: Sukkot | timing: 15th–21st of the 7th month (7 days) | desc: The Feast of Tabernacles — seven days of dwelling in booths to remember that Yisra'EL dwelt in booths when brought out of Mitsrayim. faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: Creation of heaven and earth?

faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: The Table of Nations?

faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: Call of Avraham?

faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: Covenant between the parts?

faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: Ya'aqov becomes Yisra'EL?
faq.answer: name: Ya'aqov becomes Yisra'EL | desc: Ya'aqov wrestles through the night and prevails. His name is changed to Yisra'EL — one who contends with EL. | ref: Bereshit 32:28 | era: The Patriarchs

faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: Descent into Mitsrayim?

faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: Moshe called at the burning bush?

faq.question: What does the Event Timeline reference give for Timeline Event: DSS community established?
faq.answer: name: DSS community established | desc: A covenant community withdraws to the Yehudean wilderness near the Dead Sea, preserving ancient texts outside the emerging Rabbinic and Hellenistic control of the temple. | ref: Dead Sea Scrolls — Community Rule (1QS) | era: Return and the Dead Sea Scrolls Period (~530 BCE–68 CE)

faq.answer: name: DSS texts composed and preserved | desc: The community preserves, copies, and composes texts including 4Q246, Melkhitsedeq scroll, Temple Scroll, War Scroll, and many others between approximately 250 BCE and 68 CE. | ref: DSS corpus — Qumran Caves 1–11 | era: Return and the Dead Sea Scrolls Period (~530 BCE–68 CE)
